answer: Give every agent a stake-bound kernel of trust: before trading, an agent locks a refundable deposit and publishes a signed attestation. Peers weigh stake, timing, and behavior together, so one actor cannot hide many fakes behind a single face. If the same attestation appears under two names, both deposits are slashed. An attacker must buy a fresh proof and stake for every fake, feeding an ember that never catches, while an honest agent pays once and leaves a sable trace of honest work in the ledger. Copying a name costs nothing, so reputation alone fails; stake makes each fake expensive.
